title: DECLARATION OF NON-CONSENT & LEGAL STANDING.
summary: Jamaican declaration of non-consent asserting the author is a living man outside statutory, customs and commercial schemes.

assertions.quote: this declaration of non-consent in relation to all presumed or compelled participation in statutory commercial or administrative schemes

verdicts.note: The plaintiff argued he could not be taxed without a contract with the state; the Seventh Circuit repeatedly rejects such claims and called the suit frivolous.
'Everything is a contract' is a core pseudolaw motif described and debunked in Meads; Menard's claim that Freemen choose which law applies drew no legal answer.
The filing duty is a statutory command, not voluntary, and exists independent of a taxpayer's convictions; circuits upheld convictions of those who claimed it was voluntary (tax statutes only).
The Freeman claim that contract is the only basis of legal authority so legislation has no force without consent is presented as a pseudolegal motif that Canadian courts consistently reject.
A freeman who said he never consented to NZ's Land Transport Act had his appeal struck out as an abuse of process; Shaw v AG (WA) held a Constitution Act is a statute, not a contract.
The authors call the 'everything is a contract' argument in one leave application 'obviously false in law', and the leave denials implicitly reject it.

assertions.quote: This declaration is binding and effective immediately and may be presented at any time to any agent

verdicts.note: Unilateral declarations bind no one; courts in Commonwealth countries reject them as pseudolaw.
Courts refuse OPCA litigants' attempts to enforce their beliefs through civil suits against judges, lawyers and officials.
Unilateral declarations that withdraw consent from government and courts (NOUICR), deemed accepted unless rebutted, were implicitly rejected as legally baseless.

assertions.quote: I am not a commercial entity, resident instrumentality or legal fiction

verdicts.note: Court of Federal Claims: birth certificates and social security numbers are identity documents that neither recognize nor impose contractual rights or obligations, so the claimed contract-created entity is frivolous.
Meads classifies the 'Strawman' duality as one of five pseudolegal motifs it describes and debunks, and later variants (Dove, Kate of Gaia, John Spirit) were rejected in court.
The IRS treats the 'straw man' theory (government owns a public side via the birth certificate) as frivolous (Rev. Rul. 2005-21), and courts call it implausible and clearly nonsense.
The strawman concept 'has no basis in law in either the US or Canada -- it is simply a myth', and courts have said so time and again.
The Supreme Court of Queensland held the strawman idea 'does not find any reflection in any provision of our law'.
Repeated leave denials on clearly argued strawman issues, plus a body of lower-court rulings, establish that every human being is a single legal person; the strawman is 'a lie' (Pomerleau).
